podcast.title: Debut Album (Pre-1998)
podcast.body: Semisonic's debut album received decent reviews but did not achieve significant mainstream success. "Their debut album got some decent reviews, but nothing that really catapulted them into the limelight."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Band Breakup and Reunion
podcast.body: Following a few years after their period of significant success, Semisonic disbanded. However, the band subsequently reunited in 2017, and this reunion appears to have been sustained. "after a couple of more years, Semisonic broke up. But then there was a reunion in 2017, and it seems to be sticking."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 1

podcast.title: Dan Wilson's Songwriting Prowess
podcast.body: Guitarist and singer Dan Wilson has achieved considerable recognition as a highly sought-after professional songwriter. He co-wrote Adele's massive global hit "Someone Like You," which topped charts in dozens of countries and earned him a Grammy for Song of the Year. He also received a Grammy for his production work on Adele's "21" album and was nominated for a Grammy for writing "Not Ready to Make Nice" for the Dixie Chicks. His extensive songwriting credits include collaborations with dozens of other notable acts, such as Fantagram, John Legend, Steve Perry, Josh Groban, Jason Barraiz, Leanne Rhyme, Stevie Nick's Halsey Cold War Kids, K-Flay, Weezer, Panic at the Disco, and Taylor Swift. "But the big story here is guitarist and singer Dan Wilson. He's become a renowned songwriter for hire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and Origins
podcast.body: Semisonic, like Marcy Playground, originated in Minneapolis, establishing a shared geographical root with another prominent band discussed. "Like Marcy Playground, they're also originally from Minneapolis."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: John Munson's Continued Musical Work
podcast.body: Bass player John Munson remains active in the music industry, consistently working with a variety of bands in addition to his ongoing involvement with Semisonic. "Bass player John Munson continues to work with a variety of bands in addition to Semisonic."

podcast.title: Robert Jacob Stitcher's Academic and Literary Pursuits
podcast.body: Robert Jacob Stitcher holds a degree from Harvard University in African American Studies and authored a memoir titled "So You Want to Be a Rock and Roll Star," showcasing his diverse intellectual and creative endeavors. "Robert Jacob Stitcher has a degree from Harvard in African American Studies, and he wrote a great memoir called, So You Want to Be a Rock and Roll Star."

xref.title: Breakthrough at 37 (1998)
xref.body: Dan Wilson achieved significant success at age 37, in early 1998, with Semisonic's hit song "Closing Time," after many years of trying to make it in the music industry. "When that song came out in early 1998, it quickly became a monster. And after years of trying to make it, it finally happened to Dan Wilson. He was 37."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Successful Songwriting Career
xref.body: After his success with Semisonic, Dan Wilson has had a highly lucrative career as a songwriter, earning "real money." He penned at least six songs for The Dixie Chicks (including a Grammy winner for Song of the Year), three songs for Adele's *21* album (including "Someone Like You"), and co-written with numerous other major artists such as Taylor Swift, Tom Morello, Celine Dion, John Legend, and Pink. "But it is as a songwriter where Dan has made the real money."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
